what: Verisk sells data and analytics to insurers. It holds claims and policy data contributed by the industry itself, and sells back the models insurers use to price property risk, estimate repair costs and detect fraud.
customers: Property and casualty insurers, reinsurers, brokers and repair networks, mostly in the United States.
money: rating, policy forms, catastrophe models and risk data
repair cost estimation, fraud detection and claims analytics
moat: A data pool that insurers contribute to and then pay to use, which no new entrant can recreate because the data only exists through the industry's own participation.
risks: Its customer base is concentrated in one industry
Debt of about $4.6 billion against under $1 billion of cash
Large insurers build some analytics in-house
Growth of about 7% is steady rather than fast
opportunities: Operating margin of 44% and return on invested capital of 20%
Subscription revenue renews at very high rates
Analysts see about 19% upside from current levels
watch: Organic constant-currency revenue growth and subscription renewal rates.
